To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

whole-exome sequencing revealed a missense mutation c.899G>A (p.(G300D) in the CTSC (cathepsin C) gene as the cause of Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome (PLS), a rare recessive disorder of severe periodontitis and palmo-plantar hyperkeratosis in two siblings from an Arabic family in Saudi Arabia.

1) whole-exome sequencing is a powerful tool that can be applied to identify the causative mutation in rare Mendelian disorders and can generate findings and/or inferences beyond its initial primary objective; 2) a previously reported CTSC missense mutation (c.899G>A; p.(G300D); NM_001814.4) was identified in a consanguinous PLS family and found to segregate with the disease; 3) the mutation was absent in the
a previously reported missense variant in CTSC was found in homozygosity in two siblings affected with Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome (PLS).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of genetic factors that predispose to periodontitis.
the molecular diagnosis of a rare disorder in a consanguinous family.

the use of whole exome sequencing in the diagnosis of rare genetic diseases in the context of a primary ciliary dyskinesis study and the identification of a rare mutation causing Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PLS affected children were diagnosed by a proxy molecular diagnosis using the whole-exome sequencing data of the PLS unaffected sibling.
a missense mutation, c.899G>A (p.G300D), in the CTSC (cathepsin C) gene is the molecular cause of PLS in this family.
the CTSC mutation is a rare cause of PLS in Saudi Arabia, but that the disease is likely to have a higher prevalence in the population than would otherwise be predicted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

whole-exome sequencing is a powerful tool for the identification of novel disease-causing variants and can also be used to provide a proxy molecular diagnosis of other genetic disorders in families where a second genetic disorder has been identified.

the use of whole-exome sequencing in a family with PLS led to the identification of a previously uncharacterised missense mutation in a novel candidate gene CTSC, which is likely to be causative in this family and is rare in the Saudi population.

whole exome sequencing is an effective tool for the diagnosis of rare genetic diseases in consanguineous families and can provide a proxy molecular diagnosis in families where the primary goal is not the identification of rare genetic diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
proxy molecular diagnosis is a powerful tool that can be used to diagnose a second disorder segregating in the family.
the use of whole-exome sequencing in the diagnosis of rare genetic diseases in a family can be a cost effective approach, especially when the disease is suspected but the diagnosis is elusive.
the use of whole exome sequencing in the diagnosis of rare diseases can provide valuable information about the population prevalence of the disease and can be used to make proxy molecular diagnoses.
